title: The Animal Kingdom: The Big Picture
objective: After this level you can explain what makes an animal an animal and name the main groups.
summary: An animal has many cells without walls, eats other living things and usually moves at some stage. Sponges qualify. The kingdom: five familiar groups and a vast crowd without backbones.

cards.headline: Sponges were long mistaken for plants.
cards.body: They have no muscles, and a grown sponge stays stuck to one spot for life. Only after someone noticed their small movements, in 1765, did people slowly accept sponges as animals. So what does it actually take to be an animal?

cards.headline: The animal checklist
cards.body: Biologists use a short checklist. An animal is built from many cells, and unlike plants and fungi, those cells have no cell walls. It can't make its own food, so it eats other living or dead things. And most animals can move, at least at some stage of life. Fur, legs and a face are all optional. Eating someone else's lunch is not.

mascot.line: Keep this checklist close. Level 45 runs a jellyfish through it.

cards.fact: A sponge does all its traveling as a baby.
cards.context: Sponge larvae can swim. Then they settle, attach and stay put for good. The adult feeds by pulling water through its porous body, where tiny hairlike flagella stir up currents that bring in bacteria to eat. Many cells, no cell walls, eats other living things, moved at one stage of life: a sponge ticks every box on the checklist.

items.label: The crowd you overlook
points: Worms, jellyfish, sea stars and sponges

cards.headline: Animals: defined
learned: Eats other living or dead things
Most move, at least at some life stage
Five familiar groups, plus a big crowd without backbones

questions.prompt: According to the animal checklist, animal cells lack the _____ that plant and fungus cells have.

options.label: mitochondria
options.rationale: Not on the checklist; the missing piece is the wall.

options.label: membranes
options.rationale: Every cell has one; animal cells lack walls.

options.label: DNA
options.rationale: Animal cells carry DNA; what they lack is a wall.

questions.explanation: Animal cells have no cell walls, unlike the cells of plants and fungi.

questions.prompt: Put a sponge's life in order, from first to last.
questions.explanation: Sponge larvae swim, then they settle and attach, and the adult stays put for good.

questions.prompt: Which of these belongs on the map of the animal kingdom?

options.label: A field mushroom
options.rationale: It's a fungus, and fungus cells have walls.

options.label: A seaweed
options.rationale: Seaweed makes its own food; animals must eat.

options.label: A fern
options.rationale: It's a plant, with walled cells.

questions.explanation: Jellyfish are animals without backbones, part of the big crowd beside the five familiar groups.
